STATE OF GUPTA COAL CONTRACTS

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
investigative story with new angles on the gupta coal contract Carte Blanche broke last year

Summary:
We go back to our story of June 2016 on the Optimum coal contract and show how the Eskom / Gupta party continued and we bring you new information

Further information:
In the State of Capture report, the now fired deputy finance minister Mcebisi Jonas reveals that at a meeting at the Gupta residence in Saxonwold in 2015, Ajay Gupta told him that the Gupta family does business to the value of six billion rand with government and they would like to increase that to R8 billion rand.

The rest of the story, we now know well. For refusing to accept a bag of cash, and playing by the Gupta rules, Jonas was fired by the president a few weeks ago. But for the Gupta’s their party continues and Eskom has become their money funnel.

If the Gupta’s were hoping to increase their turnover with government to R8 billion rand, they have far exceeded their own expectations! Thanks once again to Eskom. Because in a single month in 2016 – August to be precise, Eskom attempted to award the Gupta company Tegeta resources with R11 billion rand in coal contracts.


Extra Budget Items:
travelling to Mpumalanga - also may need Devi for a third day

Case Study:
matshela koko

Expert:
Mr. Peter Major Mining Investment Consultant
Mr. Hulme Scholes
Mr. xavier prevost

Locations:
gauteng nd Mpumalanga

Press Release:


Eskom Coal Contracts
Eskom has consistently denied that they have given the Gupta-owned company Tegeta Exploration and Resources any special favours. But the State of
Capture report tabled by the public protector last year, called for further investigation into their coal contracts. Now, a leaked draft, report from Treasury, has
recommended that a forensic audit firm investigates why Eskom continues to give preferential treatment to Tegeta. Carte Blanche digs into the dirty business
of coal contracts

Script:


Gupta coal final script

Commentary one
At a meeting in Saxonwold in 2015, Ajay Gupta told former deputy finance minister, Mcebisi Jonas that the Gupta family made a lot of money from the state and they would like to increase that amount from R6 billion rand to R8 billion rand. That was recorded in the State of Capture report now under review.

Well, with the help of Eskom, the Gupta company, Tegeta has exceeded their own expectations, because, in a single month last year, Eskom tried to give their company over R10 billion rand in 3 separate coal contracts

Peter
Hey, you are pushing a billion dollars here! even in the States that’s huge
money.

Commentary Two
Peter Major is a mining analyst at Cadiz

Peter
I will tell you what, if you want to ask is this a big number, think what could I do in mining? I am a mining engineer I know what I could do with R10 billion. I could create 5000 jobs, I could create 25 000 jobs with R10 billion rand!

Commentary Three
But Eskom have consistently denied that they have shown any special favours to the Gupta’s mining companies. They chose not to answer our questions because there are ongoing investigations into the contracts we have queried. But we do know how the new acting CEO of Eskom feels, because in June last year he told me.

Devi
Are you sick and tired of answering questions about the Gupta’s because these people seem to be a headache in terms of your business?
Koko
Well let me tell you what I am sick and tired of …I am sick and tired of people wanting us to treat them differently, because they are not different, because the assumption is that they cannot put an honest tender, and win it.

Commentary Four
But the uncomfortable truth, is unlike most mining companies, they don’t seem to tender yet they still get the contracts, and last year Eskom even helped Tegeta to buy the Optimum mine with a prepayment of over half a billion rand. Duduzane Zuma, the president’s son also has a stake in Tegeta

Devi
So, they bought the mine using taxpayer’s money

Peter
Well its better than using your own money, isn’t it?

Commentary five
Tegeta owns three coal mines. Brakfontein near Delmas, which has a contract to supply coal to Majuba power station; Koornfontein with a contract to supply Komati; and the Optimum mine that supplies Hendrina and Arnot, and was purchased with the help of that prepayment, Mr. Koko struggled to remember last June.

Devi
Why did Eskom prepay Optimum half a billion rand for coal?
Koko
We haven’t
Devi
You haven’t? ………
So did you prepay ….no mr Koko
Koko
……Let’s say I made a mistake …
Devi
So one of the biggest mysteries and now the allegation is this is how they were able to do it because this is as good as the money in the bank?

Commentary Six
Treasury has now said in a report the prepayment was indeed a loan.

MICHAEL RICHARDS VOICE OVER
The interest due and payable on the loan amount of R659 558 07 should be recovered from the relevant Eskom officials or Tegeta Exploration and Resources

Devi link
Remember our expose last year, where we showed how Eskom had created a fake emergency which allowed Tegeta to supply expensive coal to Arnot. Even after that debacle Eskom tried to extend that very same emergency contract by a billion rand.

Commentary seven
To be precise it was R854 million rand. But this time Eskom was stopped in its tracks by Treasury, who said no. Peter Major is astounded with the way Eskom is operating

PETER MAJOR
They are spending money without treasury authorization, they are signing deals that treasury should have oversight of.

Commentary eight
But Eskom is furious that this preliminary report, initiated under former finance minister Gordhan, was leaked a few weeks ago. It calls for a forensic audit into why Eskom continues to give Tegeta preferential treatment. Eskom complain their case is yet to be presented.




Peter
I think the scariest thing about Eskom is their sheer independence! Their audacious independence because they seem to make their own rules. They’re acting like they are their own country.

Commentary Nine
In July 2016, after our expose, then CEO Brian Molefe defended the Gupta’s.

Brian Molefe up sound
No one is telling me why we shouldn’t do business with Tegeta or the Gupta’s ..other than the fact that their bank accounts are closed or someone offered the position of minister of finance to somebody

Commentary Ten
The public protectors report on Eskom’s prepayment found it could amount to fraud, soon after Brian Molefe resigned, and Mr. Koko stepped into his job as interim CEO, meanwhile the Gupta’s coal mines began to flourish

Devi Link
When Tegeta first bought Optimum, they were saddled with a two-billion-rand penalty which you may remember Mr. Koko insisted they would pay back

KOKO
What is the status of the R2 billion-rand penalty?
Koko
It stands, we want it, it’s our money
Devi
When are you going to get that money?
Koko
Well remember they are in business rescue, as soon as it is out of BR we want it!

Devi Link
But we may never know how much was paid back, if any, because Eskom settled with them in secret a few weeks ago.

Commentary eleven
Soon after Tegeta bought Optimum, journalists were told that Tegeta had removed funds held in trust to rehabilitate the mine.

Hulme
There is no way that a minister, or the regional manager, or God can allow you to take that money out of a rehab trust after November 2015.



Commentary twelve
Specialist Mining lawyer Hulme Scholes, explains the legislation changed specifically so that mines couldn’t take the money and run and leave government to clean up after them

Hulme
The purpose of it is if you look at the Witwatersrand it looks like the surface of the moon because under old mining legislation, there was no provision so that is what they are trying to combat

Commentary Thirteen
The public protectors report confirmed that the funds had been moved into the Bank of Baroda and were being transferred between accounts

Devi
If we were to look at the optimum coal what went wrong there?

Hulme
Well the public protector report insinuates that the money has been removed from that trust and is no longer available to do final rehabilitation if that money was removed it was completely unlawful

Commentary fourteen
Inside the Optimum rehabilitation trust was R1.7 billion which was removed well after November 2015, because Tegeta only paid for Optimum mine in April 2016. Neither the department of minerals nor Oakbay have responded to our questions.

Devi
So, what are the consequences?
Hulme
The DMR can cancel your mining right under section 47, secondly the directors can be held personally liable and criminally charged for environmental consequences which arise

Commentary fifteen
Despite Mr. Koko’s assurances that Eskom doesn’t treat the Gupta’s differently, the evidence tells a different story. There is the prepayment, the removal of the rehab funds, the secret settlement of the penalty on Optimum and an attempt to extend the Arnot contract without a tender. But it doesn’t end there

Devi Link
Over there is the Koornfontein mine. In August, last year Eskom gave them a seven year, R7 billion contract to supply coal to Komati power which is just down the road, then two months later, Eskom decided to close the power station down early. So why sign the contract in the first place?

Peter Major
Now the contract is life or death. That’s what makes the coal mine so valuable nowadays more than ever is the contract

Commentary sixteen
Once again Eskom helped Tegeta. Now, if Eskom close Komati early they will have to pay out Tegeta for breaking the contract, or divert the coal. Either way, the R7 billion-rand contract has increased the value of the Gupta’s mine, should they chose to sell

Devi
Now you have your ear to the ground is it for sale
Peter
We have been told it is for sale
Devi
And when was that, recently?
Peter
Yes, it’s been in the last couple of months

Commentary seventeen
But it’s here at Brakfontein, which has a ten- year contract worth R3.8 billion rand to supply Majuba, where treasury has focused its attention and found huge irregularities

Devi Link
Where does one begin with the Brakfontein to Majuba contract. It appears there were so many contraventions, but if there is one thing that stands out it is the shocking quality of coal to Majuba

Commentary eighteen
Four months into the contract, their coal was so bad, that Eskom rejected 48% of it, and Matshela Koko suspended their contract. A week later it was lifted, but reject coal continued to flow to Majuba last year, according to a geological report seen by Carte Blanche.

Michael Richard
Unacceptable qualities delivered to Majuba included contamination (steel rubble), oversized coal, high proportions of fines and agglomerated lumps.

PETER MAJOR
I am an engineer and I just think of these things going through the silos, through the conveyer belts, through the crushers, that is why I am terrified I haven’t even thought of the financial implications.

Devi
That is the kind of coal coming out of Brakfontein

PETER MAJOR
this is beyond corruption …. What’s the word you use when you are destroying a country’s assets?



Commentary nineteen
Brakfontein’s coal is the lowest quality, yet the most expensive out of four other suppliers. Senior coal analyst Xavier Prevost looked at the specs

Xavier
The main thing and the most important is the thermal efficiency, if the carbon is low that means that a lot of the coal goes into the boiler and goes out of the boiler without being burned, and that is what happens in a case like this, instead of burning it, you are just passing it through, and decreases the thermal efficiency tremendously - it’s unburnable coal
Devi
You put it in for nothing
Xavier
Yes. You put it in and you take it out

Commentary twenty
And the reason for that says the geologist, who does not want to be named, is that this mine should never have been commissioned for Eskom in the first place.

Michael Richards
It is clear that the coal from Brakfontein does not conform to the minimum requirements of Eskom

Commentary Twenty one
But Mr. Koko had no problem with Brakfontein’s coal

Devi
So, you are clear in your mind that there is nothing wrong with Brakfontein’s coal and you will disagree with anybody, any geologists wherever they are that says that the coal quality at Brakfontein is poor?
Koko
Nonsense! The coal quality we receive at Majuba from Brakfontein complies to our specifications. Whatever gets to us, meets our quality.

Commentary twenty two
But how could Mr. Koko have known that? Eskom minutes tell how Brakfontein didn’t have an automatic sampler to measure the coal quality until the first week of June 2016, the same week we conducted this interview, and the sampler was only calibrated a few weeks later.

Devi
What would that mean if you have an automatic sampler and its not calibrated
Xavier
Well its not then reading properly

Commentary twenty three
The geologist recommends the following:


Michael Richards
The very first action to take is to terminate the Brakfontein contract immediately to get rid of the fruit salad of coal qualities

Commentary Twenty- four
But instead Eskom tried to expand Brakfontein’s contract in August last year by another R2.9 billion rand. Again, treasury said no.

So what happens next? Report after report is piling up into the affairs of Eskom, and now Mr Koko himself is under investigation for giving a billion rand’s worth of contracts to a company his stepdaughter had interests in. But Mr Koko has not been suspended and still goes to work at Megawatt Park each day.

The END Duration 14 12.

PROMO ONE
Eskom say they don’t give the Gupta mining companies any special favours, so we looked at their portfolio of three different mining contracts to see for ourselves

PROMO TWO
In a single month last year Eskom tried to give over R10 billion rand in coal contracts to Gupta mining companies
Peter
Hey, you are pushing a billion dollars here! even in the States that’s huge
money.

PROMO THREE
The Gupta owned Brakfontein mine supplies Majuba with coal. But is it acceptable quality for Eskom

PETER MAJOR
I am an engineer and I just think of these things going through the silos, through the conveyer belts, through the crushers, that is why I am terrified I haven’t even thought of the financial implications.

Michael Richards It is clear that the coal from Brakfontein does not conform to the minimum requirements of Eskom Commentary Twenty one But Mr. Koko had no problem with Brakfontein’s coal Devi So, you are clear in your mind that there is nothing wrong with Brakfontein’s coal and you will disagree with anybody, any geologists wherever they are that says that the coal quality at Brakfontein is poor? Koko Nonsense! The coal quality we receive at Majuba from Brakfontein complies to our specifications. Whatever gets to us, meets our quality. Commentary twenty two But how could Mr. Koko have known that? Eskom minutes tell how Brakfontein didn’t have an automatic sampler to measure the coal quality until the first week of June 2016, the same week we conducted this interview, and the sampler was only calibrated a few weeks later. Devi What would that mean if you have an automatic sampler and its not calibrated Xavier Well its not then reading properly Commentary twenty three The geologist recommends the following: Michael Richards The very first action to take is to terminate the Brakfontein contract immediately to get rid of the fruit salad of coal qualities Commentary Twenty- four But instead Eskom tried to expand Brakfontein’s contract in August last year by another R2.9 billion rand. Again, treasury said no. So what happens next? Report after report is piling up into the affairs of Eskom, and now Mr Koko himself is under investigation for giving a billion rand’s worth of contracts to a company his stepdaughter had interests in. But Mr Koko has not been suspended and still goes to work at Megawatt Park each day. The END Duration 14 12. PROMO ONE Eskom say they don’t give the Gupta mining companies any special favours, so we looked at their portfolio of three different mining contracts to see for ourselves PROMO TWO In a single month last year Eskom tried to give over R10 billion rand in coal contracts to Gupta mining companies Peter Hey, you are pushing a billion dollars here! even in the States that’s huge money. PROMO THREE The Gupta owned Brakfontein mine supplies Majuba with coal. But is it acceptable quality for Eskom PETER MAJOR I am an engineer and I just think of these things going through the silos, through the conveyer belts, through the crushers, that is why I am terrified I haven’t even thought of the financial implications.

metadata.Further information: In the State of Capture report, the now fired deputy finance minister Mcebisi Jonas reveals that at a meeting at the Gupta residence in Saxonwold in 2015, Ajay Gupta told him that the Gupta family does business to the value of six billion rand with government and they would like to increase that to R8 billion rand. The rest of the story, we now know well. For refusing to accept a bag of cash, and playing by the Gupta rules, Jonas was fired by the president a few weeks ago. But for the Gupta’s their party continues and Eskom has become their money funnel. If the Gupta’s were hoping to increase their turnover with government to R8 billion rand, they have far exceeded their own expectations! Thanks once again to Eskom. Because in a single month in 2016 – August to be precise, Eskom attempted to award the Gupta company Tegeta resources with R11 billion rand in coal contracts.
